title: Dry-Brined Thanksgiving Turkey With Chiles
description: A boldly spiced dry-brined Thanksgiving turkey featuring fresh and dried chiles, cumin, mint, and roasted peppers for a deeply flavorful holiday centerpiece.

ingredients.name: turkey
ingredients.quantity: 14 pounds, thawed, neck and giblets removed

ingredients.name: mixed fresh peppers
ingredients.quantity: 2 pounds (such as poblanos, jalapeños, bells, shishitos, or Cubanelles)

steps.instruction: Two to three days before roasting, pat the turkey dry and season all over, including the cavity, with coarse kosher salt.
Wrap or place the turkey in a large resealable bag, set on a sheet pan, and refrigerate for 24 to 72 hours.
The night before roasting, toast the black peppercorns, cumin seeds, and bird’s eye chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Grind the toasted spices coarsely using a mortar and pestle, spice grinder, or blender.
Mix the ground spices with dried mint, red chile powder, and 3/4 teaspoon salt to make the spice rub.
Drain any liquid from the turkey, pat it very dry, and rub the spice mixture all over the turkey and inside the cavity.
Refrigerate the uncovered turkey for 8 to 24 hours to dry the skin.
On roasting day, remove the turkey from the refrigerator 1 hour before cooking.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and place a rack in the lowest oven position.
Transfer the turkey to a roasting pan and scatter the fresh peppers and onion around it.
Stuff the cavity with fresh mint sprigs if using, tie the legs together, and tuck the wing tips under.
Brush the turkey all over with melted butter and drizzle the turkey and vegetables with olive oil.
Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F and continue roasting, rotating the pan occasionally and basting with pan juices, until the thigh reaches 165°F, about 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 hours more.
Let the turkey rest for at least 20 minutes before carving.
Serve with the roasted peppers, onions, and additional mint if desired.
